name: The Royal Dungeon
firstVisit: Rows. Rows and rows of them, in the dark, all facing the same way.
Nothing down here breathes. Something turns its head anyway.

W: Old stone, older than the castle on top of it. Cold enough to take the skin off your hand.
1: The steps back up to the Great Hall. Up there, it's only empty. Down here, it's full.
c: A torch, burning low and blue. It gives off light, and no heat at all.
k: A candle on an iron stand, set down by the Rackwarden for himself. Rest here.
X: An iron rack, cold enough to burn. A bar across the top, and a hook at about the height of a man's collar.
Like a coat stand, for something that doesn't need a coat.

objects.name: Mabb the Rackwarden
lines: Mind the rows. They don't like the rows being minded. Mind them anyway.
I count them every morning. Same number every morning. Never fewer. I don't know where he gets them.

answer: Soldiers. The king's best. They never eat, never sleep, never ask for a day off.
Never ask for anything. Never say anything. Fifteen years I've said 'good morning' to them. Nothing.
He brings them down himself. At night, a few at a time.
I asked him once. He said 'from the ground', and laughed, so I laughed. You do.
Some of them, I'd swear, I went to school with.
Tidy. The king likes things tidy. Rows. Ranks. Everything facing the same way.
Hang them up at night and they're good as new by morning. Like coats. Like very cold coats that hate you.

questions.ask: So you're a cloakroom attendant for nightmares.
answer: It's on my door. It's on my badge. My mother had it stitched on a cushion.

lines: Gone. All of them. All at once, the night the king fell.
They didn't fight it. They didn't make a sound. They just went out, row by row. Like candles.
Fifteen years of 'good morning'. One of them nodded back, at the very end. I'm choosing to believe that.
A board of tags, in the Rackwarden's neat capitals.
ROW ONE: STANDING. ROW TWO: STANDING. ROW THREE: STANDING. ROW FOUR: STANDING.
Underneath: LIGHTS OUT: NEVER. LIGHTS ON: ALSO NEVER.
The board of tags. Every row has been crossed out, and one word written underneath: GONE.
Empty racks, all down the dark. A smell like a snuffed candle.
